# Story 72 — Desk conversation view: show public replies and internal notes side-by-side (Story: CRM-103)

## Prerequisites

- **Cannot ship before** `CONVERSATION-2-API (CRM-102)` — the desk-facing endpoint that returns both public replies and internal notes in one ordered thread. This story consumes whatever shape that endpoint returns; do **not** invent fields.
- Read `.squad/plan-lessons.md` end-to-end before writing a line of code. Every listed defect that this plan repeats is grounds for rejection.
- Coordinate with the API author on the exact field name that discriminates a public reply from an internal note (`kind`, `visibility`, `type`, …) and on the field that carries the body. Do **not** guess it from this document.

---

## Story Goal

Give a desk agent a single screen for a ticket where **public replies** (visible to the customer) and **internal notes** (staff-only) are rendered together in time order, and are told apart **at a glance** — not by reading a caption. The composer at the bottom must make its current mode (public reply vs internal note) obvious **before** the agent types, so an agent about to write something they would not say to a customer knows which box they are in.

Out of scope:

- Any `api/` change — that is `CONVERSATION-2-API (CRM-102)`.
- The public/portal "my tickets" surface — that is a separate story.
- Client-side filtering of notes. **The API is the gate (SC-2).** This screen renders what it receives. A test that asserted "the screen hides notes" would be testing the wrong layer and must not be written.

## Product rules (from story)

- **SC-2** — Every rule is enforced in the API; no client enforces anything. This screen shows what the API sent.
- **BR-6** — Every visible string exists in both `en.ts` and `ar.ts` in the same commit.
- **L-51** — Any interpolated value inside a translated sentence is wrapped in U+2068 … U+2069.
- **L-55** — No native HTML validator (`type="email"`, `pattern`, `required`, `min`, `max`) on inputs whose rules the API owns.

## Implementation tasks

### 1 — New conversation page

**Create file:** `web/src/pages/conversation/ConversationPage.tsx`

- Read the ticket id from the route (`useParams`).
- Call a new `useConversation(ticketId)` hook (see task 3). Render the four states with the shared primitives:
  - `idle` / `loading` → `<Skeleton>` inside a `<Card>`.
  - `error` → `<ErrorState>`; the sentence comes from `t.conversation.errors[code]` **only after** verifying the shared `t.errors[code]` sentence is not misleading in this context (see the intake note on 401 / 429 sentences).
  - `success` with an empty thread → `<EmptyState>` with the resource string.
  - `success` with entries → a `<Stack>` of `<Card>` items, one per entry, ordered by the API's returned order (do **not** re-sort on the client; the API decides order).
- For each entry, render a visually distinct surface for **public reply** vs **internal note**:
  - Different background colour token (e.g. `--surface-default` vs `--surface-note`) and a persistent left-edge accent stripe. **The distinction is not a caption alone** (criterion: "the difference is not only a word somebody has to read").
  - A screen-reader-only label with the kind (from the resource file) so assistive tech still hears which it is.
  - Author, timestamp and body come from the API entry; interpolate through the bidi-isolate helper (see `history-sentence.ts`).
- Render `<ConversationComposer>` (task 2) below the thread.

**Create file:** `web/src/pages/conversation/ConversationPage.css`

- Two class variants for the two kinds. Colours come from `tokens.css`; add new tokens there if needed rather than hard-coding hex.

### 2 — Composer with a visible, pre-typing mode

**Create file:** `web/src/pages/conversation/ConversationComposer.tsx`

- Two-mode toggle: **Public reply** / **Internal note**. The toggle:
  - Is the **first** thing an agent sees inside the composer, above the textarea.
  - Changes the surrounding surface colour and the textarea's border/background to match the surface used in the thread for that kind. The mode is visible from the surface, not only from the toggle's label (criterion: "before they type").
  - Persists its selection in component state (default: **public reply** — the safer default is the customer-visible one, so a slip does not leak; the risky mode is the one you have to opt into).
- Textarea uses the primitive `<TextArea>`. **No native validator** (L-55). Client only checks "non-empty after trim" to disable the submit button; the API remains the authority on what constitutes a valid body.
- On submit, call the API through the hook (task 3). On `success`, clear the textarea and let the parent refetch the thread. On `error`, render the field errors from `useRequest`'s `error.fields`.
- All button labels, mode labels, placeholders and helper text come from `t.conversation.composer.*`.

### 3 — Hooks

**Create file:** `web/src/pages/conversation/useConversation.ts`

- Wraps `useRequest` for `GET` of the conversation thread endpoint owned by `CONVERSATION-2-API (CRM-102)`. Confirm the exact path from `api/src/features/conversation/conversation.routes.js` before writing it; call it via `request(...)` (which prefixes `/api/v1`).
- Returns `{ state, refetch }` where `state` matches the four-state shape.

**Create file:** `web/src/pages/conversation/usePostEntry.ts`

- Wraps `useRequest` for the POST that creates a public reply or an internal note. Accepts `{ kind, body }`. Passes both to the API verbatim — **do not** branch client-side and hit two different endpoints unless the API exposes two; use whatever `CONVERSATION-2-API (CRM-102)` defines.
- Returns `{ state, submit, reset }`.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Empty thread** — API returns zero entries. Show `<EmptyState>` with `t.conversation.emptyThread`. Do not show the thread `<Card>` list at all.
- **API omits a `kind`** — render nothing for that entry and log to console once per render; do **not** default to "public reply" (defaulting is a leak). Add a test asserting an entry with an unknown/missing kind is not rendered as a public reply.
- **Mode toggle mid-typing** — switching mode does **not** clear the textarea (the body the agent wrote is theirs). It **does** update the composer surface and the submit button label immediately so the current mode is visible at all times.
- **Rapid double-submit** — button is disabled while `usePostEntry` state is `loading`. The API is still the guarantee; the client-side disable is only a nicety.
- **Very long body** — no `maxlength` attribute (L-55 spirit). The API decides. If it returns a `fields.body` error, render that sentence.
- **RTL locale** — because interpolated values (author name, timestamps) go through the U+2068/U+2069 helper (L-51), Arabic mixed with a Latin-name author renders correctly. Add a test that flips locale to `ar` and asserts the isolates are present.
- **Signed-out session** — the route sits behind `<RequireAuth>`; if `/me` returns 401 mid-session the shared session-expiry flow handles it. Do **not** re-invent an error sentence here.
- **Fetch stub sharing a `Response`** — every test that calls `fetch` more than once must build a fresh `Response` per call (L-30).

## Test Plan

1. **`web/src/pages/conversation/ConversationPage.test.tsx`** (new, vitest + Testing Library):
   - Renders the four request states (`idle/loading/error/success/empty-success`) with stubbed `fetch` (fresh `Response` per call) and stubbed `/me` via `src/testing/stub-me.ts`.
   - Given a thread of one public reply and one internal note, asserts **both** are rendered (SC-2: the screen does not filter) and that they carry **different** surface class names / roles — not only different label text.
   - Asserts the screen-reader labels for the two kinds come from the resource file and differ.
   - Asserts Arabic rendering wraps the author name in U+2068 … U+2069.
2. **`web/src/pages/conversation/ConversationComposer.test.tsx`** (new):
   - Default mode is **public reply**.
   - The composer's surface class changes when the mode toggles — asserted **before** any text is typed (this is the "before they type" criterion).
   - Submitting posts to the endpoint with the selected `kind` and body; on `success` the textarea clears.
   - Submitting with only whitespace disables the button but the input carries no native `required` / `pattern` / `minlength` (assert the DOM does not have those attributes — L-55).
   - Error path: server returns a `fields.body` error → the sentence for that field renders.
3. **`web/src/shared/i18n/parity.test.ts`** — passes with the new `conversation` subtree added to both `en.ts` and `ar.ts` (no code change, verify).
4. **`web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts`** — passes with the new page and composer (no literal separators between tags, no bare English in JSX).
5. **`web/src/app/routing.test.tsx`** — extend to assert `/tickets/:ticketId/conversation` mounts `ConversationPage` behind auth.
6. **Do not add** a test that asserts "the page hides internal notes when the API returns them". That is testing the wrong layer (SC-2) and will be rejected.

## Verification Steps

1. **Frontend runs:** `cd web && npm test` — all new and existing vitest suites pass, including `parity.test.ts` and `no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts`.
2. **Frontend builds:** `cd web && npm run build` — `tsc -b && vite build` must succeed. `npm test` does **not** typecheck; this step is what proves the change compiles.
3. **Manual smoke:** `cd web && npm run dev`; sign in as an agent; from the queue, open a ticket's conversation; confirm the two kinds are visually distinct before reading any caption; toggle the composer mode and confirm the surface changes before typing.
4. **Regression:** `cd api && npm test` — ensure no `api/` file was touched (this story is web-only). Ownership of the enforcement remains with `CONVERSATION-2-API (CRM-102)`.
5. **No AI attribution anywhere:** `git diff --staged | grep -iE 'copilot|chatgpt|claude|assistant|ai-generated'` must return nothing. The same grep across the working tree must return nothing new.

## Done Criteria

- [ ] A ticket's public replies and internal notes render together, in the order the API returns them, on `/tickets/:ticketId/conversation`.
- [ ] The two kinds are distinguishable at a glance (surface / accent), not only by a caption.
- [ ] The composer's current mode (public reply vs internal note) is visible **before** any text is typed.
- [ ] The composer defaults to **public reply** (the customer-visible default is the safer default; the risky mode is opt-in).
- [ ] No client-side filtering of notes; a test asserting such filtering is **not** present.
- [ ] No native validators on composer inputs (L-55).
- [ ] Every visible string exists in `en.ts` and `ar.ts` (BR-6); `parity.test.ts` and `no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` pass.
- [ ] Interpolated values inside translated sentences use U+2068 / U+2069 (L-51).
- [ ] Route wired in `routes.tsx` and reachable from `TicketQueuePage.tsx`.
